summary: This theoretical work proposes a honeycomb lattice architecture for superconducting qubits with high connectivity, where each qubit is coupled via dedicated tunable couplers to a shared central mode, enabling all-to-all connectivity within unit cells. A novel single-step CZ gate protocol is introduced with gate times roughly 2× faster than prior sequential MOVE-CZ-MOVE schemes, achieving infidelities ~$6 \times 10^{-7}$ in the minimal two-qubit system.
motivation: Conventional superconducting processors use low-connectivity planar grids that require longer gate sequences and suffer from delocalization-induced crosstalk errors during simultaneous single-qubit operations. The multi-mode coupling architecture with a central element offers potential to simultaneously increase connectivity and suppress these delocalization-induced errors.
method: An effective three-mode coupling between two qubits and a shared center mode is created by simultaneously exciting states in single- and two-excitation manifolds via tunable coupler frequency pulses with Gaussian envelopes. The protocol is optimized numerically over pulse amplitudes and filter widths using full Hamiltonian simulations including all coupling modes and realistic pulse shapes.
result: For $N=2$ qubits with $\tau = 60.0$ ns gate duration, infidelity reaches $6.2 \times 10^{-7}$; including four spectator qubits increases infidelity to ~$2 \times 10^{-4}$ due to off-resonant leakage channels. Decoherence-limited fidelity at $T_1 = 30$ µs yields $1-\mathcal{F} \sim 10^{-3}$, with the protocol showing equal $T_1$ vulnerability but reduced $T_2^*$ sensitivity compared to conventional diabatic CZ gates.
